# Architecture and training objective {#app:objective}

This appendix states the policy architecture and PPO objective. We separate three implementation facts: what every policy observes, how learned messages enter the PPO update, and which architectural differences remain between learned and externally generated message-source controls.

## Observation and network architecture

For agent $i$ at round $t$, let the non-message part of the observation with temporal features be
$$
x_{i,t}
=
\bigl[
\hat f_{i,t},
\; e_i,
\; c_{t-1},
\; a_{i,t-1},
\; \mathrm{EWMA}_t
\bigr],
$$
where $\hat f_{i,t}$ is the noisy private signal, $e_i$ is the endowment, $c_{t-1}$ is the previous-round group cooperation fraction, $a_{i,t-1}$ is the agent's own previous executed action, and $\mathrm{EWMA}_t$ is an exponentially weighted moving average of recent group cooperation. The action policy observes this base vector plus the current-round message vector after the simultaneous broadcast,
$$
o^{\mathrm{act}}_{i,t}
=
\bigl[
x_{i,t},
\; \mathrm{onehot}(m_{1,t}),
\dots,
\mathrm{onehot}(m_{S,t})
\bigr],
$$
where $S=4$ is the number of sender slots. The broadcast is observed by every agent, so $o^{\mathrm{act}}_{i,t}$ includes all sender slots, including agent $i$'s own slot when $i$ is a sender. The sender head runs before the current-round broadcast, so it does not observe the current message vector. It uses the base vector plus the previous-round message vector,
$$
o^{\mathrm{msg}}_{i,t}
=
\bigl[
x_{i,t},
\; \mathrm{onehot}(m_{1,t-1}),
\dots,
\mathrm{onehot}(m_{S,t-1})
\bigr].
$$
In \texttt{no-comm}, the message block is absent. When temporal features are removed, the wrapper preserves the same tensor shape but zeros the temporal slice $(c_{t-1}, a_{i,t-1}, \mathrm{EWMA}_t)$. In communication-enabled training, message dropout is applied before received message one-hots are appended.

Let $\tilde o_{i,t} = [o^{\mathrm{act}}_{i,t};\, t/(T-1)]$ denote the action observation with an added scalar within-episode time feature. Each agent has separate feed-forward multilayer perceptrons for the action policy and value function, each with two hidden layers of width 64 and ReLU nonlinearities:
$$
\pi_i(a \mid o^{\mathrm{act}}_{i,t}) = \mathrm{Cat}\!\bigl(\mathrm{softmax}(f^{(a)}_i(o^{\mathrm{act}}_{i,t}))\bigr),
\qquad
V_i(\tilde o_{i,t}) = f^{(v)}_i(\tilde o_{i,t}),
$$
where $\mathrm{Cat}$ denotes a categorical distribution.

For learned communication, each sender has a separate message policy of the same MLP form,
$$
\psi_i^{\mathrm{msg}}(m \mid o^{\mathrm{msg}}_{i,t}) = \mathrm{Cat}\!\bigl(\mathrm{softmax}(f^{(m)}_i(o^{\mathrm{msg}}_{i,t}))\bigr),
$$
with vocabulary size $|\mathcal V|=2$. Exogenous source modes work differently: when \texttt{msg\_source\_mode} is \texttt{uniform}, \texttt{public\_random}, \texttt{fixed0}, or \texttt{fixed1}, no trainable sender message actor is instantiated. Messages are generated externally and passed through the same receiver-side wrapper. The receiver interface is matched across communication-enabled modes; only the learned mode trains a sender message policy.

## Returns and PPO objective

Agents are trained independently with generalized advantage estimation (GAE). Let $r_{i,t}$ be the reward after reward scaling, $V_i(\tilde o_{i,t})$ the value prediction, $d_t \in \{0,1\}$ the episode-termination indicator, $\gamma=0.99$ the discount factor, and $\lambda=0.95$ the GAE parameter. Here $d_t=1$ means that the transition from $t$ to $t+1$ terminates the episode. The temporal-difference residual and GAE recursion are
$$
\delta_{i,t}
=
r_{i,t}
 + \gamma (1-d_t) V_i(\tilde o_{i,t+1})
 - V_i(\tilde o_{i,t}),
$$
$$
A_{i,t}
=
\delta_{i,t}
 + \gamma \lambda (1-d_t) A_{i,t+1},
\qquad
R_{i,t} = A_{i,t} + V_i(\tilde o_{i,t}).
$$
Advantages are standardized within agent before the PPO update.

For the action policy, with PPO clip parameter $\epsilon=0.2$, the clipped ratio is
$$
r^{(a)}_{i,t}
=
\frac{\pi_i(a_{i,t}\mid o^{\mathrm{act}}_{i,t})}{\pi_i^{\mathrm{old}}(a_{i,t}\mid o^{\mathrm{act}}_{i,t})},
$$
and the action surrogate minimized by the optimizer is
$$
\mathcal L^{\mathrm{act}}_{i}
=
-\mathbb E_t
\Bigl[
\min\!\bigl(
r^{(a)}_{i,t} A_{i,t},
\mathrm{clip}(r^{(a)}_{i,t}, 1-\epsilon, 1+\epsilon) A_{i,t}
\bigr)
\Bigr].
$$

For learned senders, the message decision is updated jointly with the action decision. The message $m_{i,t}$ is sampled before the current broadcast, while the action $a_{i,t}$ is sampled after the delivered message vector has been appended to $o^{\mathrm{act}}_{i,t}$. The joint rollout probability therefore factorizes as $\psi_i^{\mathrm{msg}}(m_{i,t}\mid o^{\mathrm{msg}}_{i,t})\,\pi_i(a_{i,t}\mid o^{\mathrm{act}}_{i,t})$. On timesteps where sender $i$ emits $m_{i,t}$, the implementation forms the joint ratio
$$
r^{(a,m)}_{i,t}
=
\exp\!\Bigl(
\log \pi_i(a_{i,t}\mid o^{\mathrm{act}}_{i,t})
 + \log \psi_i^{\mathrm{msg}}(m_{i,t}\mid o^{\mathrm{msg}}_{i,t})
 - \log \pi_i^{\mathrm{old}}(a_{i,t}\mid o^{\mathrm{act}}_{i,t})
 - \log \psi_i^{\mathrm{msg,old}}(m_{i,t}\mid o^{\mathrm{msg}}_{i,t})
\Bigr),
$$
and uses the clipped joint surrogate
$$
\mathcal L^{\mathrm{joint}}_{i}
=
-\mathbb E_t
\Bigl[
\min\!\bigl(
r^{(a,m)}_{i,t} A_{i,t},
\mathrm{clip}(r^{(a,m)}_{i,t}, 1-\epsilon, 1+\epsilon) A_{i,t}
\bigr)
\Bigr].
$$
The same standardized agent-level advantage $A_{i,t}$ is used for both the action and message factors. If a minibatch contains both sender-updated and action-only samples for the same agent, the implementation averages the two surrogates in proportion to the sample counts:
$$
\mathcal L^{\mathrm{policy}}_i
=
\frac{n_i^{\mathrm{joint}}}{n_i^{\mathrm{joint}} + n_i^{\mathrm{act}}}
\mathcal L^{\mathrm{joint}}_i
+
\frac{n_i^{\mathrm{act}}}{n_i^{\mathrm{joint}} + n_i^{\mathrm{act}}}
\mathcal L^{\mathrm{act}}_i.
$$
In exogenous source-mode controls and in \texttt{no-comm}, the joint message term is absent because no trainable message actor exists.

The value loss is mean squared error,
$$
\mathcal L^{\mathrm{value}}_{i}
=
\mathbb E_t\bigl[(V_i(\tilde o_{i,t}) - R_{i,t})^2\bigr],
$$
and the action and message entropy terms are
$$
\mathcal H^{(a)}_{i,t}
=
H\!\bigl(\pi_i(\cdot \mid o^{\mathrm{act}}_{i,t})\bigr),
\qquad
\mathcal H^{(m)}_{i,t}
=
H\!\bigl(\psi_i^{\mathrm{msg}}(\cdot \mid o^{\mathrm{msg}}_{i,t})\bigr).
$$

For each agent and minibatch, the optimized loss is
$$
\mathcal L_i
=
\mathcal L^{\mathrm{policy}}_i
 + c_v \mathcal L^{\mathrm{value}}_i
 - \beta_a \, \mathbb E_t[\mathcal H^{(a)}_{i,t}]
 - \beta_m \, \mathbb E_t[\mathcal H^{(m)}_{i,t}],
$$
where $c_v=0.5$, $\mathcal L^{\mathrm{policy}}_i$ is $\mathcal L^{\mathrm{act}}_i$, $\mathcal L^{\mathrm{joint}}_i$, or their count-weighted minibatch average as described above, and the message-entropy term is present only when the agent has a learned message actor. In exogenous-source modes, $\beta_m=0$ in effect because $\mathcal H^{(m)}_{i,t}$ is absent. In the reported runs, $\beta_a$ is annealed linearly from $0.01$ to $0.001$ and $\beta_m$ from $0.01$ to $0.0$. The objective contains no positive-signalling or listening auxiliary losses.

## Remaining asymmetries across conditions

The objective contains no communication-specific auxiliary shaping, but the arms are still not identical optimization problems. Communication adds received-message inputs; learned communication adds a trainable sender head. Exogenous modes match the receiver interface but replace the sender policy with externally generated messages. Message-source controls therefore test which channel properties suffice under our training design, not whether parameterizations are identical.

## Aggregate cancellation and polarity alignment {#app:aggregate-cancellation}

The main-text interventions are causal endpoint tests. This appendix adds descriptive evidence: pooled receiver- and sender-semantics summaries can look weak even when sender-conditioned structure is strong.

These summaries are observational. They condition on message value or sender identity under the policy's natural rollout, so they describe endpoint structure and convention fragmentation but cannot identify what a forced intervention would do.

For the diagnostics below, we compare the aggregate received-token effect for receiver $j$,
$$
  \delta_{\mathrm{agg}}(\fhat_{\mathrm{bin}}) =
  P(C_j \mid \exists\, k \ne j: m_k=1,\fhat_{\mathrm{bin}})
  -
  P(C_j \mid \forall\, k \ne j: m_k=0,\fhat_{\mathrm{bin}})
$$
to the sender-conditioned effect, for $i \ne j$,
$$
  \delta_{i \rightarrow j}(\fhat_{\mathrm{bin}}) =
  P(C_j \mid m_i=1,\fhat_{\mathrm{bin}})
  -
  P(C_j \mid m_i=0,\fhat_{\mathrm{bin}}).
$$
For sender polarity, we summarize each sender's endpoint convention by
$$
  \Delta_{\mathrm{high-low}} =
  P(m_i=1 \mid \fhat \ge 4.5) - P(m_i=1 \mid \fhat < 1.5),
$$
These extreme private-signal bins summarize coarse polarity and are not intended as pure true-regime labels. We then ask whether different senders share the same sign or split into opposite polarities.

These $\fhat$-bin averages differ from the true-regime-conditioned any-token effects in Section \ref{sec-sender-probes}. Ratios are computed from unrounded values. Mean $\pm$ SEM over 15 seeds.",

## Grouped surrogate specification {#app:lowdim-spec}

Parallel to Section \ref{sec-lowdim}, this appendix asks whether sender-indexed message features generalize across independently trained populations. It is not a causal test. The target is the receiver's binary action on natural frozen traces from the learned communication policy, filtered to \texttt{cond1}, \texttt{ablation=none}, \texttt{history\_intervention=none}, and checkpoint 150k. For each focal multiplier, we subsample at most 5,000 observations per training seed; grouped 5-fold cross-validation holds out entire seeds, so each fold tests whether a mapping learned on some populations predicts behavior in unseen ones.

All surrogate models use the same pipeline as the analysis code: standardized numeric inputs, one-hot categorical inputs, and a \texttt{liblinear} logistic regression with \texttt{max\_iter=2000}. The models differ only in how the message stream is encoded:

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
print(
    render_table_here(
        "tbl-lowdim-spec",
        r"Exact grouped-surrogate specification for Section \ref{sec-lowdim}. All models predict the receiver's action on natural frozen traces at 150k. Numeric columns are standardized; categorical columns are one-hot encoded. Grouped 5-fold cross-validation holds out entire training seeds. The only change across rows is the message encoding.",
        render_lowdim_spec_table(),
    )
)
```

The full-pattern variable \texttt{pattern} is receiver-indexed: it records which specific senders delivered which bits to that receiver, so it can express sender-specific conventions. Poor held-out performance of \texttt{history\_pattern} therefore means these detailed sender-indexed mappings do not transfer across independently trained seeds, even though they matter within a seed.

This appendix reports the full cross-seed transfer tests from Section \ref{sec-lowdim}, including seedwise detail and provenance. For each receiver seed, we transplant a donor seed's learned message stream while keeping the receiver policy fixed. The matched suite uses the same evaluation seed for raw foreign identity and the global $0 \leftrightarrow 1$ flip, and reports ordered-pair and receiver-level summaries for those two streams only.

## Sender-encoding decomposition {#app:sender-encoding}

The traces record each sender's eventual intended action directly, so the action-linked effect uses intended cooperation/defection, not executed action. Unlike the extreme-bin polarity statistic in Appendix \ref{app:aggregate-cancellation}, the regime-linked effect here uses the task-relevant cooperation-threshold split, $\hat f < 3.5$ versus $\hat f \ge 3.5$. For the sensitivity check below, a sender-seed pair is labeled \emph{mixed} if both the regime-linked and action-linked mean absolute effects clear threshold $\tau$, \emph{regime-leaning} if only the regime effect clears it, \emph{action-leaning} if only the action effect clears it, and \emph{weak or unclear} otherwise.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from collections import defaultdict
from matplotlib.patches import Rectangle
from matplotlib.colors import TwoSlopeNorm

sender_ids = sorted(set(row["sender_id"] for row in SENDER_CAUSAL_MATRIX_ROWS))
receiver_ids = sorted(set(row["receiver_id"] for row in SENDER_CAUSAL_MATRIX_ROWS))
f_panels = [("3.5", r"$f=3.5$"), ("5.0", r"$f=5.0$")]

pair_signed = defaultdict(list)
for row in SENDER_CAUSAL_MATRIX_ROWS:
    key = (row["true_f"], row["sender_id"], row["receiver_id"])
    pair_signed[key].append(float(row["delta_p_cooperate_1_minus_0"]) * 100.0)

signed_panels = []
for f_value, _ in f_panels:
    panel = []
    for sender_id in sender_ids:
        row_values = []
        for receiver_id in receiver_ids:
            vals = pair_signed[(f_value, sender_id, receiver_id)]
            row_values.append(sum(vals) / len(vals))
        panel.append(row_values)
    signed_panels.append(panel)

signed_vmax = max(abs(value) for panel in signed_panels for row in panel for value in row)
signed_norm = TwoSlopeNorm(vmin=-signed_vmax, vcenter=0.0, vmax=signed_vmax)

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(5.6, 2.25), constrained_layout=True)
for idx, (ax, panel, (_, title)) in enumerate(zip(axes, signed_panels, f_panels)):
    im = ax.imshow(panel, cmap="RdBu_r", norm=signed_norm)
    ax.set_title(title, fontsize=9)
    ax.set_xticks(range(len(receiver_ids)))
    ax.set_xticklabels([rid.replace("agent_", "A") for rid in receiver_ids], fontsize=8)
    ax.set_yticks(range(len(sender_ids)))
    ax.set_yticklabels([sid.replace("agent_", "A") for sid in sender_ids], fontsize=8)
    ax.set_xlabel("Receiver")
    if idx == 0:
        ax.set_ylabel("Sender")
    for i in range(len(sender_ids)):
        for j in range(len(receiver_ids)):
            color = "white" if abs(panel[i][j]) > 0.55 * signed_vmax else "black"
            ax.text(j, i, f"{panel[i][j]:+.1f}", ha="center", va="center", fontsize=7.5, color=color)
        ax.add_patch(Rectangle((i - 0.5, i - 0.5), 1, 1, fill=False, edgecolor="black", linewidth=1.0))

cbar = fig.colorbar(im, ax=axes.ravel().tolist(), shrink=0.88)
cbar.set_label(r"Mean $\Delta P(C)$ (pp)", fontsize=8)
cbar.ax.tick_params(labelsize=7)

signed_sender_fig_path = GENERATED_FIG_ROOT / "fig-sender-probe-signed.pdf"
fig.savefig(signed_sender_fig_path, bbox_inches="tight")
plt.close(fig)
print(
    render_figure_here(
        "fig-sender-probe-signed",
        r"Cross-seed cancellation of signed sender-probe effects. Each heatmap cell shows the signed mean change in receiver cooperation when forcing one sender's token to 1 rather than 0, averaged across 15 seeds. Because sender polarities differ across seeds, positive and negative effects can cancel; small signed means indicate direction instability rather than absence of within-seed receiver influence. Figure \ref{fig-endpoint-panels} shows absolute effect magnitudes.",
        signed_sender_fig_path,
        width=r"0.76\linewidth",
        position="H",
    )
)
```

# Observation-noise sweep {#app:noise}

The noise sweep tests whether the communication advantage changes when private signal quality varies at evaluation time. Agents were trained at $\sigma = 0.5$; we evaluate at $\sigma \in \{0.0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0\}$. Table \ref{tbl-noise} shows the $f=5.0$ panel; the $f=3.5$ gap is also non-monotone in $\sigma$ and shaped differently.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
print(
    render_table_here(
        "tbl-noise",
        r"Communication retains a large advantage across the full evaluation-time noise sweep, and the gap is larger under the noisiest observations than under perfect information. Cooperation rates at $f=5.0$ under varying evaluation-time noise $\sigma$ (agents were trained at $\sigma=0.5$). The non-monotone middle rows show that this is an endpoint sensitivity check rather than a calibrated psychometric curve, but the larger gap at $\sigma=1.0$ than $\sigma=0$ is consistent with messages carrying regime information when private signals are unreliable.",
        render_noise_table(),
    )
)
```

The sweep changes observation noise only at evaluation. It is endpoint sensitivity, not evidence about how communication would develop under different training noise.

### Design note {#app:msgsource-provenance}

The message-source comparison is only interpretable when the receiver interface and training objective are held fixed. Changing both the message source and other training details would obscure the mechanism, so the main interpretation rests on contrasts within the matched design.

# Reproducibility details {#app:repro}

The reported training runs use independent PPO with 4 agents, horizon $T=100$, 8 parallel environments counted in environment episodes, two 64-unit hidden layers, learning rate $3\times 10^{-4}$, $\gamma=0.99$, $\lambda=0.95$, clip ratio $0.2$, value-loss coefficient $0.5$, max-grad-norm $0.5$, and reward scaling by 20.0. Communication runs use a binary vocabulary, 4 sender slots, message dropout 0.1, linear action-entropy annealing from 0.01 to 0.001, linear message-entropy annealing from 0.01 to 0, and no positive-signalling or listening auxiliary losses.

Across experiments, the environment uses endowment 4.0, multiplier set $\{0.5, 1.5, 2.5, 3.5, 5.0\}$, private-noise standard deviations $(0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5)$, regime persistence $\rho=0.05$, and tremble probability 0.05. Main claims are based on 15 training seeds per condition with checkpoints at 25k, 50k, 100k, and 150k episodes; reported evaluation summaries are greedy means over those 15 seeds unless a table or caption says otherwise. The software stack targets Python 3.10 with PyTorch 2.10.0 and PettingZoo 1.18.1.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
from datetime import datetime
import re

COMPUTE_BATCH_LOGS = {
    "comm_full_clean_learned": ARTIFACTS["message_source_train_learned"] / "status" / "progress.log",
    "comm_reduced_zeroaux": ZEROAUX_COMM_REDUCED_ROOT / "status" / "progress.log",
    "nocomm_full_canonical": ARTIFACTS["factorial_without_comm_full_history"] / "status" / "progress.log",
    "nocomm_reduced_canonical": ARTIFACTS["factorial_without_comm_reduced_history"] / "status" / "progress.log",
    "clean_uniform": ARTIFACTS["message_source_train_uniform"] / "status" / "progress.log",
    "clean_public_random": ARTIFACTS["message_source_train_public_random"] / "status" / "progress.log",
    "clean_fixed0": ARTIFACTS["message_source_train_fixed0"] / "status" / "progress.log",
    "clean_fixed1": ARTIFACTS["message_source_train_fixed1"] / "status" / "progress.log",
}


def progress_batch_stats(path):
    lines = Path(path).read_text().splitlines()
    ts_re = re.compile(r"^\[(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2} \d{2}:\d{2}:\d{2})\]")
    train_start = train_end = None
    max_parallel = None
    for line in lines:
        if "train batch start" in line or "batch start" in line:
            match = ts_re.match(line)
            if match:
                train_start = datetime.strptime(match.group(1), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")
            mp = re.search(r"max_parallel=(\d+)", line)
            if mp:
                max_parallel = int(mp.group(1))
        elif "train batch done" in line or "batch done" in line:
            match = ts_re.match(line)
            if match:
                train_end = datetime.strptime(match.group(1), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")
    if train_start is None or train_end is None or max_parallel is None:
        raise ValueError(f"incomplete batch log: {path}")
    batch_hours = (train_end - train_start).total_seconds() / 3600.0
    active_seed_processes = min(max_parallel, 15)
    seed_hours = batch_hours if active_seed_processes >= 15 else batch_hours * active_seed_processes / 15.0
    worker_hours = batch_hours * active_seed_processes
    return {
        "batch_hours": batch_hours,
        "seed_hours": seed_hours,
        "worker_hours": worker_hours,
        "active_seed_processes": active_seed_processes,
        "max_parallel": max_parallel,
    }


compute_stats = {name: progress_batch_stats(path) for name, path in COMPUTE_BATCH_LOGS.items()}
clean_names = ("comm_full_clean_learned", "clean_uniform", "clean_public_random", "clean_fixed0", "clean_fixed1")
factorial_names = (
    "comm_full_clean_learned",
    "comm_reduced_zeroaux",
    "nocomm_full_canonical",
    "nocomm_reduced_canonical",
)
clean_batch_hours = [compute_stats[name]["batch_hours"] for name in clean_names]
factorial_batch_hours = [compute_stats[name]["batch_hours"] for name in factorial_names]
factorial_seed_hours = [compute_stats[name]["seed_hours"] for name in factorial_names]
timed_worker_hours = sum(stats["worker_hours"] for stats in compute_stats.values())

print(
    f"Approximate wall-clock from batch logs is as follows. The learned-communication arm with temporal features uses the clean zero-aux message-source run and took about {fmt_num(compute_stats['comm_full_clean_learned']['batch_hours'], 1)} h with {compute_stats['comm_full_clean_learned']['active_seed_processes']} active seed processes. The zero-aux communication arm without temporal features took about {fmt_num(compute_stats['comm_reduced_zeroaux']['batch_hours'], 1)} h with {compute_stats['comm_reduced_zeroaux']['active_seed_processes']} active seed processes. The canonical no-communication baselines with and without temporal features took {fmt_num(compute_stats['nocomm_full_canonical']['batch_hours'], 1)} h and {fmt_num(compute_stats['nocomm_reduced_canonical']['batch_hours'], 1)} h, respectively, with {compute_stats['nocomm_full_canonical']['active_seed_processes']} active seed processes. The matched message-source controls used 15 active seed processes; 15-seed training batches took {fmt_num(min(clean_batch_hours), 1)}--{fmt_num(max(clean_batch_hours), 1)} h depending on mode. Across the unique timed batches, these reported training runs account for about {fmt_num(timed_worker_hours, 0)} seed-worker-hours. The no-communication baselines have no message channel, so communication-specific shaping terms are inactive for those arms."
)
```

These are approximate wall-clock disclosures from batch logs, not CPU-core accounting. The logs record parallelism but not per-job peak memory; the compute disclosure is approximate, not exhaustive.

# Broader impacts {#app:broader}

This paper studies evaluation of emergent communication in a stylized social dilemma. Its main positive impact is scientific: sharper tests for distinguishing portable communication from shared-cue effects, and a clearer view of evaluation failures that can mislead MARL research. Better diagnosis of when messages are portable could improve how coordination systems are benchmarked.

Possible negative impacts are indirect but real. Techniques that make agent coordination more effective or make message channels easier to exploit could be adapted in larger strategic multi-agent systems, including settings where strong coordination is undesirable. A more immediate risk is scientific overclaiming: if brittle, population-specific conventions are mistaken for portable shared protocols, researchers may deploy or interpret learned communication systems with more confidence than the evidence warrants.

\clearpage

## Game and training

This appendix reports the second case study, which tests whether the framework gives different profiles in a structurally different setting. The task is a four-agent hidden-need role-allocation game. A hidden binary need state is observed only via local noisy signals. Each round, a hidden role lottery assigns one informed but ineligible agent (low-noise need signal, prohibitive volunteer cost), two capable but uninformed agents (eligible, costs drawn from $\{0.5, 0.9, 1.3, 1.7\}$), and one mostly-ineligible distractor. Volunteering pays a cost regardless of outcome; the efficient pattern is exactly one low-cost eligible volunteer when need is present and none when need is absent.

Welfare is per-round mean payoff averaged over agents and rounds; Table \ref{tbl-role-allocation-conditions} reports the no-communication baseline for scale. Information and ability are deliberately separated: random or fixed messages cannot condition volunteering on the hidden need state, in contrast to EPGG. Senders emit one of three symbols; training and evaluation otherwise mirror EPGG (independent PPO, 15 seeds, greedy evaluation); the anonymized review artifact includes the full role-allocation config.
